title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Grothendieck proves a lemma. Let M be a category with a homotopy interval structure, stable under finite sums, with those sums universal. Then the passage to the homotopy category, M -> W_h^{-1}M (here written \overline{Cat} for M = (Cat)), commutes with finite sums. The proof runs as follows. Two maps out of a coproduct are homotopic iff their components are. Given finitely many components, one can choose a single composite interval I_N, long enough to carry all the component homotopies at once. Since I x (coprod X_j) = coprod (I x X_j), these glue to one homotopy.

This page: the NB records that the finiteness hypothesis is essential. The functor (Cat) -> \overline{Cat} = (Cat)/homotopy (homotopy being the equivalence relation generated by natural transformations) seems not to commute with infinite sums.

Counterexample:
- Take X_n = Delta_0 (the point) for all n in N, so coprod X_n is the discrete category N.
- Let Y = I_infty = (-> <- -> <- ...), the infinite zigzag. It is the amalgamated sum of infinitely many copies of Delta_1 glued end to end.
- Let f_n, g_n : X_n -> Y be the base vertex 0 and the vertex n.
- Each pair f_n, g_n is homotopic, but only through a chain of about n elementary homotopies. A natural transformation between functors pt -> I_infty moves the image one step along an arrow.
- A homotopy between f = (f_n) and g = (g_n) on coprod X_n is a finite chain of elementary homotopies, equivalently one homotopy parametrized by a finite composite interval I_N. Such a chain moves each point at most N steps.
- Hence f and g are not homotopic, although all their components are.

So Hom_{\overline{Cat}}(coprod X_n, Y) -> prod Hom_{\overline{Cat}}(X_n, Y) is not injective, and coprod X_n is not a coproduct in \overline{Cat}. Grothendieck starts to assert more strongly that the X_n have no sum at all in \overline{Cat} ('car ...'), but leaves it unjustified.

He then conjectures ('??') that in Hot(W), the localization of Cat at the weak equivalences W (the true homotopy category, not the naive homotopy quotient), arbitrary sums exist and Cat -> Hot(W) commutes with them. The next page reformulates this as bijectivity of Hom_Hot(coprod X_j, Y) -> prod Hom_Hot(X_j, Y). He worries that with the calculus of fractions neither injectivity nor surjectivity is clear, since a common target Y -> Y' in W for infinitely many fractions is not evident (only for finite subfamilies, via filtered pro-objects).

The page thus distinguishes the 'strict' homotopy category (quotient by homotopy, defined via intervals) from the localization, at the level of infinite colimits.
errors: No mathematical error in the counterexample: it correctly shows non-injectivity of the comparison map in Cat/homotopy, because homotopies of uniform finite length cannot connect points at unbounded zigzag distance.

Gap: the (partly struck or underlined) stronger claim that the family X_n has no coproduct at all in \overline{Cat} is left without proof ('car ...'). Failure of the obvious candidate does not by itself exclude some other coproduct object.

The conjecture about Hot(W) is correct, but no argument is given. For the standard W (Thomason weak equivalences) it follows from the nerve preserving coproducts and weak equivalences being stable under coproducts. For general basic or fundamental localizers it is proved in the later literature, not here.

ideas.what: Naive homotopy quotient of Cat (via interval / natural-transformation homotopies) fails to preserve infinite coproducts, because homotopies would need unbounded length; counterexample with the infinite zigzag I_infty
ideas.modern_name: Failure of the classical homotopy category (homotopy-classes quotient) to have infinite coproducts; non-uniform homotopy length
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; the phenomenon of unbounded zigzag length in Cat-homotopy is standard (e.g. in the discussion of Thomason's model structure and of 'homotopy interval' structures)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses homotopy interval structures and composite intervals; unsure whether this exact counterexample appears there

ideas.what: Finite sums are preserved by M -> W_h^{-1}M for homotopy interval structures (composite intervals I_N), from the previous page, used here as contrast
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy category of an interval/cylinder structure commutes with finite coproducts
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (homotopy interval sections) - unsure of exact statement

ideas.what: Conjecture: Hot(W) has arbitrary sums and Cat -> Hot(W) preserves them
ideas.modern_name: Localization at a (basic/fundamental) localizer commutes with small coproducts; coproducts are homotopy coproducts
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thomason (1980) for the standard case via model structure; Cisinski (Astérisque 308) and Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301) for general Grothendieck localizers
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs / Pursuing Stacks treat basic localizers; Maltsiniotis' exposition of Grothendieck's homotopy theory

missed.claim: Grothendieck asserts, without completing the argument, that the family of points has no coproduct at all in \overline{Cat} = Cat/homotopy, not merely that Cat -> \overline{Cat} fails to preserve it. This is a small, apparently unchecked categorical question.
missed.quote: les X_n n'ont pas une somme dans \overline{Cat}, car ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: it would sharpen the contrast between naive homotopy quotients and localizations. It is of little research importance.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, standard counterexample (unbounded zigzag length) plus a conjecture that is now well known to be true. It is useful as a document of Grothendieck's reasoning but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 6 likely reads 'suite d'un nombre croissant d'homotopies él[émentaires]' (an increasing number of elementary homotopies).

The line before 'une somme dans \overline{Cat}' seems to read '[-les-] X_n n'ont pas une somme dans \overline{Cat},' with 'n'ont pas' underlined (emphasis) rather than struck. That is, he claims the X_n have no coproduct in \overline{Cat}, followed by an unfinished 'car'.
'Je suppose néanmoins' is a plausible reading of the line beginning 'Je suppose...'.
